tiers.write: Changes what the viewer shows; no files are read or written.
tiers.file: Reads or writes data outside the viewer (structure files, images).

conventions: Verbs: get_* and find read; set_* change the active structure or view in place; build_* make a new row and select it; run_* start a job; export_* and save_image write files. Atom-addressed commands take atoms (0-based indices) or selection (a find id, "user", "all"). A row id is passed and returned as structure (inside get_state's structure and structures it is id). Results are objects; structural edits return atomCount and revision. Units: Å, eV and fractional coordinates carry no suffix; other units are suffixed (K, Fs, GPa, Pct, THz, S). Errors are {code, message, details}; INVALID_ARGS names the argument. "mcp": false marks commands for the Python Viewer only.
revisionGuard: Every command accepts expectedRevision (get_state's structure.revision): it then runs only if the active structure is unchanged since, and otherwise fails with STRUCTURE_CHANGED (current revision and atom count). The MCP server lists it on the commands marked "guard": true (they edit by atom index). The revision covers atom identity, species and the cell, not positions: moving atoms never renumbers them.

commands.name: get_state
commands.description: What the viewer shows now, including changes the user made by hand. Always: structure (the active one: id, name, frame, frames, atomCount, revision, formula, composition, periodic, lattice vectors and a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma, positionsCommitted, hiddenCount) and renderer. revision is a token that changes with any structural edit (atoms added, removed or re-elemented, the cell), the user's or yours, never with a colour or a move: pass it as expectedRevision to edits by atom index. include picks the other sections (default camera, selection, jobs): structures (every loaded row: id, name, frames, active, activeFrame), camera (direction from the view centre to the camera, the convention set_view takes; screen up; distance; zoom; orthographic or perspective), selection (the atoms the user has selected), jobs (id, kind, status; runs started from the Atomistic and EOS windows too), colors (each element's colour and the atoms with their own colour, grouped by colour), phonons (the loaded phonon data: q-points, labelled path points, bands, frequencies in THz at the selected q-point or Γ, the mode, amplitude, speed, length unit), field (volumetric fields: labels and, for the shown one, iso level, data min/max, grid), windows (every window: ref window:<id> for read_window and click_control, title, open). selection carries origin {by, atom} when known: by "pick" is a click on one atom (atom is the clicked atom); marquee, focus-region, row-click, host and others selected a group at once (atom null). Atom lists come from find.

include.description: Sections besides structure and renderer. Default [camera, selection, jobs].

commands.name: find
commands.description: Pick out atoms, bonds, polyhedra or voids of the active structure. Atoms, bonds and polyhedra are kept as a selection (id) for apply, remove_atoms, set_element and move_atoms; voids are places, so they get none. Every kind but voids takes where.in / where.notIn (selection ids, one or a list): only atoms in all of the first and none of the second (a polyhedra selection's atoms are its centres and corners). atoms: where {element or elements, indices, frac: {min: [x,y,z], max: [x,y,z]} (fractional box, periodic; min > max wraps through 0), near: {point: [x,y,z] fractional | atom: index, within: Å}}; items [index, element, fractional position]. bonds: every bond of the periodic structure under the get_bonding rule, drawn or not (cells up to 3000 atoms), where {elements: [A, B], minLength, maxLength}; items [a, b, image, length], b's copy being at its fractional position + image relative to a; each bond once. With where.atoms (centre indices), bonds lists each centre's neighbours instead: items [centre, neighbour, image, length], nearest first. polyhedra: where {type: centered|cage, center: element, cn}; computed on demand when they are not shown. voids: interstitial sites, largest first, where {minRadius}; items {position (fractional, on a 0.4 Å grid), radius (Å to the nearest atom), neighbours (the first shell, e.g. 12 O for a perovskite A site)}: put an atom there with add_atoms. fields: "indices" returns only the atom indices; groupBy: "element" returns counts and indices per element (both keep a big structure small). count is always the full number. A selection stays valid while the same atoms sit at the same indices (element changes and moves keep it); adding or removing atoms, or a supercell, makes it stale: find again. For heavy analysis on many atoms (rings, graph searches), use export_structure and get_bonding and run your own script, then act with atom indices.

where.description: Filters; each kind takes only its own keys (others are refused). atoms: element(s), indices, frac, near, in, notIn. bonds: elements (a pair), atoms (centres: their neighbour lists), minLength, maxLength, in, notIn. polyhedra: type, center, cn, in, notIn. voids: minRadius.

limit.description: Items to return, default 100; count is always the full number.

fields.description: items (default): details per item; indices: only the atom indices.

groupBy.description: Counts and atom indices per element.

commands.name: get_bonding
commands.description: The bond rule CrysViz draws bonds with: per element pair present, min and max cutoff (Å, including the user's edits) and whether the pair is shown, plus the exact rule. With export_structure, a script reproduces CrysViz's bonds exactly (e.g. to find rings) instead of another program's defaults.

commands.name: get_symmetry
commands.description: Space group of the active structure at a tolerance, as the Symmetry window reads it (Moyo): number, Hermann-Mauguin symbol, Hall number, Pearson symbol, and the number of atoms per Wyckoff letter (listAtoms: true gives their indices). Hidden atoms are left out (hiddenExcluded says how many). Call at two tolerances to see how robust the symmetry is.

tolerance.description: Symmetry tolerance in Å (symprec). Default: the app's setting.

listAtoms.description: Give the atom indices per Wyckoff letter, not just counts. Default false.

commands.name: search_controls
commands.description: Find any window, action or labelled control (button, toggle, slider, choice, field) in CrysViz by what it does, as the app's own feature search does: 'bonds', 'detect cages', 'atom size', 'lattice vibrations'. End the query with on or off ('bonds off', 'polyhedra on') to put the matching toggles first. Returns {count, controls: [{ref, type, kind, label, path}]}; the refs go to get_control, set_control and click_control. Use this for anything no other tool covers.

commands.name: get_control
commands.description: The current state of a control from search_controls: on/off for a toggle, value and range for a slider or field, value and options for a choice. Opens the control's window if it is not open.

commands.name: set_control
commands.description: Set a control from search_controls as a user would, so the app reacts exactly as to the user: true/false for a toggle, a number for a slider or number field, an option value or label for a choice, text for a text field. Returns the control's new state.

value.description: true/false, a number, or a string, depending on the control.

commands.name: click_control
commands.description: Press a button, open a window or run an action from search_controls, as a user's click would. The result says what happened: the control's state, effects (windowsOpened, windowsClosed, dialogsOpened with title and short text) and, when the click saved files through the app's Download or Save path, savedFiles with their absolute paths (in a host window, downloads go to the download folder: the export folder under crysviz-mcp).

commands.name: read_window
commands.description: Read a window's status line and visible text (up to 4000 characters), opening it if needed: the fallback for a result that is only shown in a window. Prefer a command's own structured result when there is one. panel is a window ref (window:<id>, from get_state include ["windows"] or search_controls) or the bare id (e.g. eos, symmetry, phonon).

panel.description: Window ref or id, e.g. "window:eos" or "eos".

commands.name: select_structure
commands.description: Show a loaded row (and one of its frames): it becomes the active structure the other commands act on. structure is a row id (get_state include structures lists them; build_* and jobs return theirs). Returns the row as build_* do: {structure, name, frames, activeFrame, atomCount, revision}.

commands.name: add_atoms
commands.description: Add atoms to the active structure at fractional positions, as the Add Atom window does; they get the next indices. Refuses atoms closer than 0.5 Å to another atom (details list the pairs) unless force is true. Returns {added, atomCount, revision}.

element.description: Element symbol, or Va for a vacancy.

force.description: Add even when atoms are closer than 0.5 Å.

commands.name: remove_atoms
commands.description: Delete atoms from the active structure, as the structure editor does. Indices of the atoms after them shift down. The result lists each removed atom's index, element, fractional position and occupancy, so add_atoms can put them back (undo), with the new atomCount and revision.

atoms.description: Atom indices (0-based, structure order), instead of selection.

selection.description: A find selection id, "user" (what the user has selected in the window) or "all".

commands.name: revert_structure
commands.description: Put the active structure back as it was loaded, discarding every edit since (moved, added, removed and re-elemented atoms, the lattice), as the Modify Structure window's Revert Changes does, without its confirm. As loaded is the structure's own snapshot from when it was created: for a file, as read, so a supercell is undone too (set_supercell again if wanted); a row made by build_* or a job reverts to how it was made. A Wyckoff lock is dropped. Returns {reverted, revision, atomCount}; a structure with no snapshot returns applied: false.

commands.name: set_element
commands.description: Change atoms to another element in place, as an element edit in the structure editor: index, position and identity stay, so nothing is renumbered and selections stay valid. An atom with its own colour keeps it; one at its element's default colour takes the new element's default. Ordered sites only (a disordered site's species are edited in the structure editor). Returns {changed, element, atomCount, revision}.

element.description: Element symbol, or Va for a vacancy.

atoms.description: Atom indices (0-based, structure order), instead of selection.

selection.description: A find selection id, "user" (what the user has selected in the window) or "all".

commands.name: move_atoms
commands.description: Move atoms of the active structure: to (one position per atom, in the order of atoms or the selection) or by (one shift for all). Fractional unless cartesian is true (then Å). Committed as a coordinate edit in the Modify Structure window: bonds and polyhedra are rebuilt and an open window shows the new positions. Moves never renumber atoms. Returns {moved, committed (always true), atomCount, revision}.

atoms.description: Atom indices (0-based, structure order), instead of selection.

selection.description: A find selection id, "user" (what the user has selected in the window) or "all".

cartesian.description: to/by in Å instead of fractional. Default false.

commit.description: No effect, kept for older callers: every move is committed.

commands.name: set_lattice
commands.description: Replace the lattice vectors of the active structure (rows a, b, c in Å); atoms keep their fractional positions. Committed as a lattice edit in the Modify Structure window. Returns the new cell parameters with atomCount and revision.

commands.name: set_supercell
commands.description: Show the active structure as a supercell, its cell repeated n = [nx, ny, nz] times, as the Cell & Supercell window does (in place: atoms are renumbered, so selections go stale). [1, 1, 1] goes back to the original cell. The window remembers it for this structure and restores it on the next load. Returns {supercell, atomCount, revision}.

commands.name: update_fractional_positions
commands.description: Python Viewer only: replace the fractional positions of every atom (MCP has move_atoms).

positions.description: One [x, y, z] fractional position per atom, in atom order.

commit.description: Also rebuild bonds and derived data, default false.

commands.name: commit_positions
commands.description: Python Viewer only: rebuild bonds and derived data after update_fractional_positions with commit false.

commands.name: build_slab
commands.description: Cut a surface slab from the active (ordered) crystal along (h k l) as a new, selected row: `layers` repeats of the stacking period (for fcc (111) one repeat is one atomic layer; for (100) of a conventional cell it is two), with `vacuum` Å as one gap along the surface normal (c is made perpendicular to the surface, slab centred). Returns the row as select_structure does, plus layers, thickness and c (Å). View it side-on with set_view x or y.

commands.name: build_symmetrized
commands.description: Standardise the active structure at a tolerance into a new, selected row, as the Symmetry window's Conv. Cell / Prim. Cell buttons do: atoms snapped to the space group's ideal sites in the conventional (default) or primitive cell. The original row is kept. Returns the row as select_structure does, plus number and symbol; then export_structure writes it out.

tolerance.description: Symmetry tolerance in Å (symprec). Default: the app's setting.

commands.name: build_phonon_frames
commands.description: The phonon mode chosen with set_phonon as `count` frames over one period (at the current or given amplitude), as a new, selected trajectory row. select_structure {structure, frame} and save_image each frame for a picture series. Returns the row as select_structure does, plus amplitude.

commands.name: set_view
commands.description: Set the camera in one call, in this order: direction (look along a lattice vector a, b, c, a Cartesian axis x, y, z or a lattice direction [u, v, w]), up (which way is up on screen), zoom, then rotate (orbit about a world axis) and recenter (bring the structure to the middle, rotation and zoom kept). Give only what should change: up or zoom alone keep the current direction. For a tilted view give a direction such as [1, 0.2, 0.1]. With cartesian: true, arrays are Cartesian, so get_state's camera direction and up restore a view. Returns the camera as get_state reports it.

direction.description: "a", "b", "c", "x", "y", "z", or [u, v, w] meaning u*a + v*b + w*c.

up.description: Which way is up on screen, in the same forms as direction; only its part perpendicular to the view direction counts.

zoom.description: Camera zoom; 1 fits the structure as loaded, larger is closer. Matches get_state's zoom.

cartesian.description: Read direction and up arrays as Cartesian x, y, z instead of lattice [u, v, w]. Default false.

recenter.description: Bring the structure back to the middle.

commands.name: set_renderer
commands.description: Switch the renderer. raytrace and pathtrace are progressive tracers (slower; no transparent background). Returns {renderer}.

commands.name: apply
commands.description: Act on atoms: atoms (indices, structure order, as find, get_state and export_structure's order use) or selection (a find id, "user" for what the user has selected in the window, "all"). action: highlight (glow), select (the app's selection, which the Selection Inspector and measuring use; it replaces the user's, and the result says what it replaced), clear (what: highlight (default) or selection: the selection is the user's too, so it is cleared only when asked), color (color '#rrggbb', every copy of each atom, kept for the session), reset_color (back to the element colour; on selection "all", the Atoms tab's Reset Colors for atoms, bonds, polyhedra and arrows), hide, show. A bonds selection acts on its atoms; a drawn polyhedra selection's color colours the polyhedra themselves (for their atoms: find atoms where {in: <that selection>}). bondPair: [A, B] with color colours every A-B bond. Returns {action, kind, count}.

atoms.description: Atom indices (0-based, structure order), instead of selection.

selection.description: A find selection id, "user" (what the user has selected in the window) or "all".

bondPair.description: With color: two element symbols; colours every bond of that pair.

commands.name: set_phonon
commands.description: Show and animate phonon modes (data loaded from a phonopy band.yaml, mesh.yaml or qpoints.yaml with load), as the Phonons window does: a mode (qpoint: index, "Gamma" or a band-path label; band: index or "lowest_optical", the first band above the three acoustic ones), the animation (animate: play, pause, or stop, which returns atoms to equilibrium), amplitude (largest atomic excursion, Å) and speed (cycles per second). Give only what should change; a new mode plays unless animate says otherwise. get_state include phonons lists the q-points and frequencies.

qpoint.description: Index, "Gamma", or a label from get_state's phonons.

commands.name: set_isosurface
commands.description: Set the isosurface level of a volumetric field, as typing it in the Volumetric Field window does (clamped to the data range). Values are in the file's units (CHGCAR: e/Å³ after the app's volume normalisation).

field.description: A label from get_state's field; default the shown field.

commands.name: add_plane
commands.description: Add a Crystal Planes plane with Miller indices hkl, as the Crystal Planes window does: through an atom (throughAtom), at offset Å along its normal, or (default) the first lattice plane. show: "field" colours it with a volumetric field (a 2D slice; field picks which), "plane" (default) draws it plain. cut hides the atoms along or opposite the normal. Returns {hkl, normal, d, show, cut, field, planeCount}.

field.description: With show: field, a label from get_state's field.

commands.name: run_md
commands.description: Start molecular dynamics on the active structure with the Atomistic window's potential (default NEP89, 89 elements) or the one potential picks, as the MD window's start does: velocity Verlet with a Bussi thermostat (NVT), or with a barostat (NPT). The frames go to a new trajectory row, selected when the run ends. A job: it returns {jobId, kind, status, progress, elapsedS} at once (or with its result if it ends within waitS); follow it with wait_job. One calculation at a time. The result names the trajectory {structure, name, frames}. symmetry: true keeps the space group during the run.

timestepFs.description: Default: recommended for the elements (shorter with H).

saveStride.description: Save a trajectory frame every this many steps. Default 4.

symmetry.description: Keep the space group: lock the structure to its symmetry first, as the Symmetry window's Enable Wyckoff Editor does (a lock already on is kept). true, or {tolerance} in Å (default: the app's symmetry tolerance). The result's symmetry says which group was locked and whether it still holds at the end. A structure whose symmetry cannot be found is refused (applied: false).

potential.description: The potential, picked as in the Atomistic window's Choose potential (the window shows the switch, and it stays picked): nep (NEP89), pet-mad (PET-MAD, the model chosen in the window), ase (the connected ASE server's model; refused with POTENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE when no server is connected). Default: the window's current choice (NEP unless the user changed it). The result's potential names the one used.

waitS.description: Wait up to this many seconds for the job to end before returning (default 0: return at once).

commands.name: run_relax
commands.description: Start relaxing the active structure with the Atomistic window's potential (default NEP89) or the one potential picks, as the Relax button does: atoms (and the cell, unless relaxCell is false) move until every force is below fmax (eV/Å) and the pressure is within pressureTolGPa of pressureGPa. A job, as run_md. The result: targetPressureGPa and relaxCell it used (and a pressureHint when the structure's name mentions a different pressure: a hint only), the new trajectory {structure, name, frames} (its last frame is the relaxed structure and is shown; the source row is unchanged), steps, converged, stopped, fmax, energy and energyPerAtom (eV), pressureGPa. To compare before and after, export_structure both (structure, frame) and diff them in a script. To continue an unconverged relaxation, call run_relax again: it starts from the structure on show, the relaxed last frame, with maxSteps more steps.

relaxCell.description: Also relax the cell. Default true.

pressureGPa.description: Target pressure for the cell, GPa. Default 0.

symmetry.description: Keep the space group: lock the structure to its symmetry first, as the Symmetry window's Enable Wyckoff Editor does (a lock already on is kept). true, or {tolerance} in Å (default: the app's symmetry tolerance). The result's symmetry says which group was locked and whether it still holds at the end. A structure whose symmetry cannot be found is refused (applied: false).

potential.description: The potential, picked as in the Atomistic window's Choose potential (the window shows the switch, and it stays picked): nep (NEP89), pet-mad (PET-MAD, the model chosen in the window), ase (the connected ASE server's model; refused with POTENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE when no server is connected). Default: the window's current choice (NEP unless the user changed it). The result's potential names the one used.

waitS.description: Wait up to this many seconds for the job to end before returning (default 0: return at once).

commands.name: run_energy
commands.description: Single-point energy, forces and pressure of the active structure with the Atomistic window's potential (or the one potential picks), as the window's EFS button does (forces show as arrows if Forces are on). A job, as run_md (it may first load the potential; waitS 25 usually returns the result in one call). Result: potential, energy, energyPerAtom (eV), fmax (eV/Å), pressureGPa.

potential.description: The potential, picked as in the Atomistic window's Choose potential (the window shows the switch, and it stays picked): nep (NEP89), pet-mad (PET-MAD, the model chosen in the window), ase (the connected ASE server's model; refused with POTENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE when no server is connected). Default: the window's current choice (NEP unless the user changed it). The result's potential names the one used.

waitS.description: Wait up to this many seconds for the job to end before returning (default 0: return at once).

commands.name: run_eos
commands.description: Equation of state of the active structure with the Atomistic window's potential (or the one potential picks), fitted (3rd-order Birch–Murnaghan) and shown in the EOS Fitting window. Scan by volume (volumeRangePct: cell volumes over ±that %, cell fixed, atoms relaxed) or by pressure (pMinGPa..pMaxGPa, cell relaxed to each, the window's own mode). Relax first: the volume scan centres on the current cell. A job, as run_md. The result has every point (volumes Å³ per cell, energies eV, pressuresGPa) and the fit: E0 (eV), V0 (Å³ per cell), B0GPa, B0Prime from the E–V and P–V fits. The fit needs SciPy via Pyodide, fetched from the network on first use. The result starts with fitReliable and warnings: when fitReliable is false (points not converged, the minimum not bracketed, no zero pressure in the scan, V0 outside the scanned volumes, B0 or B0' unphysical), the fit numbers are not a result; tell the user why instead of reporting them.

volumeRangePct.description: Scan by volume: ±this % around the current cell volume.

pMinGPa.description: Scan by pressure (when volumeRangePct is not given). Default -2.

fmax.description: Force tolerance per point, eV/Å. Default 0.01.

symmetry.description: Keep the space group: lock the structure to its symmetry first, as the Symmetry window's Enable Wyckoff Editor does (a lock already on is kept). true, or {tolerance} in Å (default: the app's symmetry tolerance). The result's symmetry says which group was locked and whether it still holds at the end. A structure whose symmetry cannot be found is refused (applied: false).

potential.description: The potential, picked as in the Atomistic window's Choose potential (the window shows the switch, and it stays picked): nep (NEP89), pet-mad (PET-MAD, the model chosen in the window), ase (the connected ASE server's model; refused with POTENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE when no server is connected). Default: the window's current choice (NEP unless the user changed it). The result's potential names the one used.

waitS.description: Wait up to this many seconds for the job to end before returning (default 0: return at once).

commands.name: run_ordering
commands.description: Ordered approximants of a disordered structure (fractionally occupied sites), as the Order Structure section of Cell & Supercell does: `samples` random decorations in a cell `multiplier` times larger, each scored with a single-point energy with the Atomistic window's potential or the one potential picks (unless energies is false), kept as one new trajectory row sorted lowest energy first. A job, as run_md. The result lists each frame's seed and energyPerAtom (eV); frame 0 is the lowest (select_structure {structure, frame: 0}).

multiplier.description: Cell size factor, as the window's Size choice. Default 1.

potential.description: The potential, picked as in the Atomistic window's Choose potential (the window shows the switch, and it stays picked): nep (NEP89), pet-mad (PET-MAD, the model chosen in the window), ase (the connected ASE server's model; refused with POTENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE when no server is connected). Default: the window's current choice (NEP unless the user changed it). The result's potential names the one used.

waitS.description: Wait up to this many seconds for the job to end before returning (default 0: return at once).

commands.name: wait_job
commands.description: Wait until a job ends or waitS seconds pass (at most 25; 0 just reports), then return it: {jobId, kind, status (running, done, failed, cancelled), progress, elapsedS, result or error once it ended, active: the structure and frame on show afterwards}. Call again while it is still running.

waitS.description: Default 20; 0 is a status check. The same name as the run_* tools use.

commands.name: cancel_job
commands.description: Stop a running job after its current step, also one the user started from the Atomistic or EOS window (their Stop buttons do the same to yours). An MD run keeps the frames it saved.

commands.name: load
commands.wire: Wire form: the browser receives name plus the file as data (fetched from the host). The MCP tool and Viewer.load take a path or text instead (src/crysviz/_mcp.py LOAD_SCHEMA).
commands.description: Load a structure file (CIF, POSCAR, XYZ, extxyz and the other formats CrysViz reads) and make it the active structure.

name.description: File name; its extension selects the format unless format is given.

format.description: Format name overriding the file extension.

periodic.description: Force the structure to be treated as periodic or not.

interactive.description: false skips load-time questions (CIF symmetry) and loads the structure as written. Default true.

commands.name: save_image
commands.wire: Wire form: the browser renders and uploads the PNG to a managed output URL the Python host adds. The MCP tool adds filename and returnImage (src/crysviz/_mcp.py SAVE_IMAGE_SCHEMA); Viewer.save_image takes a path.
commands.description: Render the current view, as the user has framed it, to PNG or SVG. Without width and height it is the view's own size and aspect; with one of them the other follows the view's aspect. The camera is never moved. format svg is the Download Image window's SVG export: the structure as an embedded image with labels, axes and colour bars as editable layers, or with vector: true as vector shapes (large for big views). PNG size: one GPU render surface (the driver's limit, often 4096 to 8192 px a side, and the Settings > Graphics GPU memory budget); raster renderers tile larger images, and when the GPU cannot allocate a surface the error says what it got, so ask for less.

maxSide.description: Scale a default (view-sized) image down to fit this side.

structureOnly.description: Hide the cell, axes and other helpers.

vector.description: svg only: atoms and bonds as vector shapes instead of an embedded image.

commands.name: export_structure
commands.wire: Wire form: the browser writes the text and uploads it to a managed output URL the Python host adds. The MCP tool adds filename (export folder); Viewer.export_structure takes a path.
commands.description: Write a structure file. cif and poscar write one frame as the Save window does (cif keeps partial occupancy; poscar groups atoms by element, so the result gives order: file atom k is CrysViz atom order[k], or sameOrder when identical). extxyz writes frames (all of the row by default) with Lattice, species, Cartesian positions (Å), energy and MD step, for ASE, pymatgen or OVITO scripts (e.g. a mean-squared displacement after run_md). structure and frame pick a row and frame other than the one on show, without selecting it.

structure.description: Row id; default the row on show.

frame.description: Frame; default the one on show.
